title: bug: collectTaskPathTiers throws on a truthy non-iterable step file list and splits a string into characters
description: Repro (probe in a Linux snapshot, found by task-f943b687): util/attributionTiers.ts collectTaskPathTiers spreads `[...(step.affectedFiles || []), ...(step.newFiles || []), ...(step.modifiedFiles || [])]`. With newFiles: 7 or {a:1} it throws "(step.newFiles || []) is not iterable", which fails get_commit_scope for EVERY task that has that peer; with newFiles: 'src/str.ts' it plans the characters 's','r','c','t'. The header and get_commit_scope promise a peer's junk never fails another task's scope. Fix with Array.isArray guards (null/false already tolerated) plus a test; completedStepFiles has the same unguarded `s.modifiedFiles || s.affectedFiles || []` flatMap.
definitionOfDone: collectTaskPathTiers and collectAssertedPaths return the valid entries and never throw for a non-array affectedFiles/newFiles/modifiedFiles (number, object, string)
Tests pin each shape in attributionTiers.test.ts and one get_commit_scope case with a junk peer

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/attributionTiers.test.ts. It is pure and needs no harness: build Task objects cast through unknown. Use exact toEqual, and add expect(() => ...).not.toThrow() wherever it applies.

1. Step lists.
   - For each field (affectedFiles, newFiles, modifiedFiles) and each junk value (7, {a:1}, 'src/str.ts'), use it.each over a PENDING step whose other two lists are valid, e.g. affectedFiles ['ok/a.ts'].
   - collectTaskPathTiers returns exactly the valid entries in `planned`.
   - It contains no single-character path: 's', 'r', 'c' or '.' never appear.
2. Completed steps (completedStepFiles, through collectAssertedPaths). It keeps completeTask.ts's selection, `modifiedFiles || affectedFiles`, and guards what that selects:
   - modifiedFiles junk with affectedFiles ['ok/b.ts'] contributes NOTHING, because the truthy junk is selected and is not an array;
   - modifiedFiles undefined with affectedFiles junk contributes nothing;
   - valid modifiedFiles contributes exactly its entries.
3. Task-level lists. filesModified, declaredFiles, touchedFiles and inferredPaths set to 7, {a:1} or 'abc' contribute nothing, and nothing throws. collectDeclaredPaths returns [].
4. Commits.
   - `commits` of 7, {a:1} or 'x' contributes nothing.
   - [7, null, {paths: 'p.ts'}, {paths: ['ok/c.ts'], inferredPaths: 'ok/c.ts'}] asserts exactly ['ok/c.ts']. The junk inferredPaths string is ignored, so it removes nothing.
5. Plan shape. implementationPlan [null, 7, 'step', {status: 'COMPLETED', affectedFiles: ['ok/d.ts']}] skips the non-objects and asserts ['ok/d.ts'].
6. Control: one well-formed task gives the exact asserted and planned tiers it gives today.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts, add ONE case next to 'does not throw on junk step data and adds no entry for it', reusing that block's setupLanding and scope helpers.
- The peer has a step with newFiles 7, modifiedFiles {a:1} and affectedFiles 'src/str.ts', plus declaredFiles ['ok/peer.ts'].
- The caller's scope succeeds.
- The peer contributes exactly ['ok/peer.ts'] to peerDeclared, and no character paths.

Red proof: in the Linux snapshot (step 3's recipe), run `npx vitest run src/util/attributionTiers.test.ts src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts`.
- The 7 and {a:1} rows throw 'is not iterable'.
- The string rows show character paths.
- The control and the existing cases pass.
Record it.

Error handling in tests: each row asserts no throw, as well as the exact result.
implementationPlan.note: Red proof in Linux snapshot (/tmp/moe-7e39.*): 38 failures, incl. 'is not iterable' TypeErrors for 7/{a:1} and string rows; getCommitScope junk-peer case throws. Existing cases pass. Many dirty peer paths in shared tree left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix packages/moe-daemon/src/util/attributionTiers.ts with ONE guard used for every list it reads.

- Add `function asList(value: unknown): readonly unknown[]`, returning `Array.isArray(value) ? value : []`.
- PathSet.addAll takes `raws: unknown` and iterates only an array. Every caller (getCommitScope.ts:61/140-142/235, recordCommit.ts:339 and this module) already passes arrays, so getCommitScope.ts and recordCommit.ts need no edit. Their task-level reads become junk-safe for free.
- planSteps: `asList(task.implementationPlan)` keeping only non-null, non-array objects.
- completedStepFiles: `.flatMap((s) => asList(s.modifiedFiles || s.affectedFiles))`.
  - This is exactly completeTask.ts's selection, with only a non-array result contributing nothing.
  - Update its JSDoc to say so: the mirror agrees on every well-formed record, and completeTask.ts itself is unchanged.
- nonInferredCommitPaths: `asList(commit.paths)`.
- collectAssertedPaths: `for (const commit of asList(task.commits))`, skipping a commit that is not a non-null object.
- collectTaskPathTiers: `[...asList(step.affectedFiles), ...asList(step.newFiles), ...asList(step.modifiedFiles)]` and `asList(task.inferredPaths)`.
- Header comment: extend the 'DROPPED rather than thrown' sentence. A list field that is not an array contributes nothing: it is never spread, and never iterated as characters.

Error handling: every read in this module is total over arbitrary JSON, so no input shape throws. Valid entries keep today's normalization, dedupe and order.
implementationPlan.note: asList/isRecord guards; addAll takes unknown; green in snapshot: 2 files, 103 tests pass, tsc clean.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Guard only the three step-list spreads named in the report. Rejected: the same module also throws on, or splits, non-array task-level lists (filesModified, declaredFiles, touchedFiles, inferredPaths, commits, commit.paths/inferredPaths) and on non-object plan steps. Its header promises that a peer's junk never fails another task's scope. One asList guard plus a guarded PathSet.addAll closes all of them in the same file.
- Make completedStepFiles fall back to affectedFiles when modifiedFiles is junk. Rejected: that would make it disagree with completeTask.ts's `modifiedFiles || affectedFiles` selection. Keeping the selection and guarding the selected value keeps the mirror honest.
- Also changing completeTask.ts. Rejected as out of scope: it only reads the caller's own record.

- collectTaskPathTiers and collectPeerPaths feed get_commit_scope's PEER map for EVERY other open task. collectAssertedPaths feeds get_context's declaredPaths.

- util/attributionTiers.test.ts does not exist yet.
